Updated - November 28, 2026 03:29 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram
The Delimitation Bill will reduce the political representation of the south Indian States and destroy the federal system in the country, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said.
His statement comes against the backdrop of the Union government convening a special sitting of Parliament where it is likely to table an amended delimitation Bill.
The Minister, in a statement on Saturday (November 28, 2026), said the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was implementing its agenda of political interests and cementing power. Its aim was to increase the political dominance of north Indian States and weaken the voice of the south Indian States in Parliament. This was a challenge to the country’s unity and democracy, the Congress leader said.
The BJP’s claim that the aim of redrawing constituencies was to ensure 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha was incorrect. It was trying to undermine democracy in the country and impose the Sangh Parivar agenda. It approach was to punish the south Indian States that were a model in population control, social development, health, and education.
All south Indian States should stand together on the issue of delimitation. The Congress would stage strong protests to protect the rights of States and ensure equal justice in a democratic system, Mr. Chennithala said in the statement.
